title: The Legendary Ladder
audit_comment: THE MONSTER TAIL of DMO Chapter 2 (printed pp. 57-66): the altering-monsters doctrine (the +/-1/2/3 modifier applied throughout, the hit-point and damage floors, the THACO and save deltas with the 20 ceiling and the 3 floor, the XP floor at 1-1, the unchanged characteristics, the size-shift option), the six ability-score grids of Tables 6-11 (13 roll bands by the size and intelligence columns, the exceptional-strength encoding, the rust monster reads), and the eleven legendary-rank tables 12-22 (the AC and hit-die ladder with the area multiplier, the breath averages and sizes, the disease onset and fatality dice, the fear radius and saves, the crush dice, the wounding bleed, the melee bonuses, the movement percentages, the gaze saves, the magic resistance, the regeneration rates with the lesser-scion delay).
audit_anchor: // ---- R227: the wis mental save wiring audit ----
prev_record: the table half of DMO Chapter 2:
rows x 5 cols: roll count, die
and the quirks boxes closed. Spec

banner.title: THE LEGENDARY LADDER - DMO Chapter 2 closes: the altering-monsters doctrine (the +/-1/2/3 modifier used throughout - hit points floored at one a die, damage at one a die, saves capped at 20 and floored at 3, XP floored at 1-1, THACO and AC moved the printed way, movement and Intelligence and alignment and morale untouched, the three-point size shift optional), the ability-scores system (3d6 read by Size and Intelligence - Tables 6-11, the warrior bonuses, the total-not-per-die damage rule, the weight-allowance bumps 35/70/105, the bend-bars ladder, the three-point language gap), and the legendary ranks (Lesser Scion through Paragon - the AC -4 to -12 and hit-dice +5 to +25 ladder with the x1.5 through x3.5 area multiplier, the rank ability rolls 3d4+4 through 1d8+10, the power counts two-to-three through five-to-seven).
banner.provenance: verified against printed pp. 57-66 of the uploaded DMO session capture (part 1, printed page N at OCR page N+1); the scrag colony example from p. 57, the rust monster reads from p. 58, the rank rosters and Table 12 from p. 61, the breath and disease and fear and crush tables from pp. 62-63, the wounding and melee and movement and gaze and resistance and regeneration tables from pp. 64-66.
banner.sentinel: the gap census after this round: 37 closed, 59 open - ALL EIGHTEEN monster boxes of Chapter 2 close and the chapter is DONE; the DMO arc continues with Chapter 3 (Spells and Magical Items, pp. 68-85).

consts.name: denAbilityRowCount

consts.name: denRankCount
consts.comment: the legendary-rank count: five ranks - Lesser Scion, Scion, Elder, Great Elder, Paragon (printed p. 61, Table 12).

consts.name: denAlterMax
consts.comment: the altering-monsters cap: the modifier applied to a weaker or stronger specimen is -1, -2 or -3, or +1, +2 or +3 (printed p. 57).

consts.name: denHpFloor
consts.comment: the weaker-monster hit-point floor: the modifier is subtracted from each hit die, but the creature always receives at least one hit point from each hit die (printed p. 57).

consts.name: denDamageFloor
consts.comment: the weaker-monster damage floor: the modifier is subtracted from each damage die, but the creature inflicts at least one point of damage with each die (printed p. 57).

consts.name: denSaveCeiling
consts.comment: the weaker-monster save ceiling: the modifier is added to the base saving throws, but no saving throw can be increased above 20 (printed p. 57).

consts.name: denSaveFloor
consts.comment: the stronger-monster save floor: the modifier is subtracted from the saving throw numbers, but no saving throw can be reduced below 3 (printed p. 57).

consts.name: denXpHdFloor
consts.comment: the weaker-monster XP floor: the modifier is subtracted from the adjusted hit dice for the XP value, but no creature can have a value lower than 1-1 (printed p. 57).

consts.name: denSizeShiftModifier
consts.comment: the optional size shift: a +3 modifier can bump the creature to the next higher size class and a -3 can reduce it one step (printed p. 57).

consts.name: denAbilityRollDie
consts.comment: the ability-score generation die: roll 3d6 on the appropriate table and read the result from the applicable column (printed p. 58).

consts.name: denAbilityRollCount
consts.comment: the ability-score generation roll count: three dice of the d6 (printed p. 58).

consts.name: denWeightAllowLarge
consts.comment: the monster weight allowance bump, large: add 35 pounds to a large creature's weight allowance - the higher of this and any listed capacity (printed p. 58).

consts.name: denWeightAllowHuge
consts.comment: the monster weight allowance bump, huge: add 70 pounds (printed p. 58).

consts.name: denWeightAllowGargantuan
consts.comment: the monster weight allowance bump, gargantuan: add 105 pounds (printed p. 58).

consts.name: denBendBarsLargePct
consts.comment: the monster bend bars/lift gates bonus, large: +5 percent - exceptionally sturdy objects negate the bonus (printed p. 59).

consts.name: denBendBarsHugePct
consts.comment: the monster bend bars/lift gates bonus, huge: +10 percent (printed p. 59).

consts.name: denBendBarsGargantuanPct
consts.comment: the monster bend bars/lift gates bonus, gargantuan: +20 percent (printed p. 59).

consts.name: denLanguageGap
consts.comment: the monster language gap: a creature with an Intelligence score at least three points higher than the normal value for its race can understand one or more languages - the hoof-tap horse (printed p. 59).

consts.name: denScionRollCount

consts.name: denScionRollBonus

consts.name: denElderPowersMax
consts.comment: the elder power range, maximum: three to five powers (printed p. 61).

consts.name: denElderRollCount

consts.name: denElderRollBonus

consts.name: denGreatElderPowersMax
consts.comment: the great elder power range, maximum: four to six powers (printed p. 61).

consts.name: denParagonPowersMin

consts.name: denParagonPowersMax
consts.comment: the paragon power range, maximum: five to seven powers (printed p. 61).

consts.name: denParagonRollDie

consts.name: denFixedHpPerExtraDie

consts.name: denBreathPerDayMin

consts.name: denBreathWaitRoundsMax

consts.name: denParagonBreathHalfPerHd
consts.comment: the paragon breath rule in half-points: an existing breath weapon averages 4.5 points of damage per hit die - the 39-hit-die paragon dragon turtle inflicts an average of 175 (printed p. 62).

consts.name: denAvgD4Half

consts.name: denCloudHeightFt

consts.name: denLineHeightFt
consts.comment: the breath line geometry, height: 5 feet tall (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denDiseaseCheckDie
consts.comment: the cause-disease check: after a successful physical attack roll 1d100 - equal to or less than the damage inflicted contracts the disease; two hits for 17 and 21 points means 38 or less, checked once a round (printed p. 62).

consts.name: denChillsRoundsDie
consts.comment: the chills duration die: the victim shivers 2d4 rounds, unable to move, attack or cast spells (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denChillsRoundsCount
consts.comment: the chills duration count: two dice of the d4, recurring on a fresh onset roll (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denChillsPenalty
consts.comment: the chills penalty: all saving throws and ability checks suffer -4 while the chills last (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denDeliriumSnapRoll
consts.comment: the delirium snap-out roll: once each turn the victim snaps out on a 9 or less on 1d20, the Constitution hit-point adjustment applying as bonus or penalty (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denFeverConsciousRoll
consts.comment: the fever consciousness roll: forced into action the victim rolls a 9 or less on 1d20 each hour to stay conscious, else delirium 2d4 rounds and a stupor 2d4 hours (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denCauseFearHdMax
consts.comment: the cause-fear panic bar: creatures of less than 4+1 hit dice flee on sight when the monster attacks or charges (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denCauseFearLevelMax
consts.comment: the cause-fear panic bar, characters: 4th level or less (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denCauseFearFleeDie
consts.comment: the cause-fear flee duration die: panicked creatures flee 2d4 turns as though under the 4th-level wizard fear spell (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denCauseFearFleeCount
consts.comment: the cause-fear flee duration count: two dice of the d4, in turns (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denCrushHeightMin
consts.comment: the flying crush height: a flying creature or one jumping down from 30 feet or more can crush at the end of its movement (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denCrushTwoSizePenalty
consts.comment: the crush save penalty, two sizes smaller: the save vs. death is at -4 (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denCrushThreeSizePenalty
consts.comment: the crush save penalty, three sizes smaller: -8, and so on down the sizes (printed p. 63).

consts.name: denExistingGazeParagonPenalty
consts.comment: the existing-gaze-weapon rule: use the next higher rank's values - a paragon's gaze penalty is -8 (printed p. 66).

bools.name: denSameModifierThroughout
bools.comment: the altering-monsters constancy doctrine: once you start altering a monster, use the same modifier throughout the process (printed p. 57).

bools.name: denUnchangedCharacteristics
bools.comment: the altering-monsters scope doctrine: the creature's movement rate, Intelligence, alignment, morale and other statistics remain unchanged under the modifier system (printed p. 57).

bools.name: denAbilityWarriorBonuses
bools.comment: the monster ability doctrine, strength: except as noted, all modifiers apply to creatures as they do for characters, and creatures gain the warrior combat bonuses for high scores (printed p. 58).

bools.name: denDamageTotalNotPerDie
bools.comment: the monster ability doctrine, damage adjustment: the bonus or penalty applies to the creature's natural attacks - if the creature rolls multiple dice the adjustment applies to the total, not each die (printed p. 58).

bools.name: denDexMovesBonus
bools.comment: the monster ability doctrine, dexterity: all modifiers apply as for characters, except the Reaction Adjustment also increases the movement rate (printed p. 59).

bools.name: denNonhumanoidDoctrine
bools.comment: the ability-scores-for-monsters scope: the system is intended for nonhumanoid creatures (humanoids are best treated as characters) but works with any creature in a pinch; the Size and Intelligence ratings determine the range (printed pp. 57-58).

bools.name: denRankPotencyDoctrine
bools.comment: the legendary potency doctrine: like a dragon's fear radius, a legendary monster's power potency is based on its overall rank - an elder's breath is noticeably deadlier than a lesser scion's (printed p. 62).

bools.name: denExistingBreathNextRank
bools.comment: the existing-breath-weapon rule: a creature that already has a breath weapon uses the values for the next higher rank, and all damaging breath weapons deal half on a successful save (printed p. 62).

bools.name: denGazeEffortless
bools.comment: the gaze-attack doctrine: a gaze attack requires no special effort and freely combines with other attacks and abilities - the effect is whatever the DM desires, with the save to avoid it (printed p. 66).

bools.name: denCrushFullMovement
bools.comment: the crush-attack doctrine: the creature expends its full movement allowance for the round and takes no other actions; opponents larger than the attacker cannot be crushed (printed p. 63).

bools.name: denCrushOverrunNoAoo
bools.comment: the crush-and-overrun doctrine: under the PLAYER'S OPTION overrun rule a crush attack does not provoke an attack of opportunity, knocked-down creatures smaller than the attacker can be trampled, and overruns work only against smaller creatures (printed p. 63).

bools.name: denWoundNoRegen
bools.comment: the wounding doctrine: wounds from this power cannot be healed by regeneration, first aid, or any magical means short of a wish, a 10th-level healing spell, or a periapt of wound closure (printed p. 64).

bools.name: denLesserRegenBar
bools.comment: the lesser-regeneration bar: a scion or lesser scion eventually regenerates any damage unless attacked with fire, acid, or magical wounding, and cannot regenerate back to life after a disintegrate or death-magic kill, or if its remains are destroyed (printed p. 66).

bools.name: denEnhancedMovementRoundsUp
bools.comment: the enhanced-movement doctrine: the normal movement increases by the listed percentage with fractions rounded up, and the bonus also defines unusual movement powers - leaps, blinks, climbs (printed p. 66).

tables.name: denResist

tables.name: denRegen
tables.comment: the Table 22 grid (printed p. 66): five ranks; the hit points regained each melee round and the lesser-scion delay - no hit points regained until three rounds after the first wound.
col_comments: the Table 22 hit points regenerated per round for the rank (printed p. 66).
the Table 22 regeneration delay in rounds after the first wound - the lesser scion's printed three, 0 elsewhere (printed p. 66).

table_checks.note: the rust monster strength read: a man-sized creature, a roll of 10 lands in the 9-12 band, the M column gives Strength 12 (printed p. 58)
the rust monster intelligence read: a roll of 18 in the A column gives Intelligence 4 - an Einstein among rust monsters (printed p. 58)
the scrag chief: a +3 specimen adds three per hit die - HD 5+20 from 5+5, the +3 riding every die and the damage dice floored (printed p. 57)
the elder hydra head: 8 hp a head x the elder 2.5 multiplier = 20 (printed p. 61)
the paragon dragon turtle: 39 hit dice x 4.5 = 175.5, the printed average 175 in half-points (printed p. 62)
the disease example: two hits for 17 and 21 points - the victim contracts on 38 or less, the damage summed before the 1d100 check (printed p. 62)
the great elder chimera: +3 per die and one extra die - the 2d3+6 claws and the 4d4+12 tail (printed p. 65)
the scion displacer beast: 15 base movement + 30 percent rounds to 20 (printed p. 66)
the lesser scion breath: 26-35 average damage at a -2 save, the gorgon-class petrifying breath (printed pp. 62-63)

the lesser scion regeneration delay: no hit points until three rounds after the first wound - the troll rule riding the legendary ladder; the paragon regenerates 4 a round with no delay (printed p. 66)
the weight allowance ladder: 35, 70 and 105 pounds by size (printed p. 58)
the bend bars ladder: +5, +10 and +20 percent by size, sturdy objects negating the bonus (printed p. 59)
